statement.essentials: The removed tissue is marked so the pathologist knows which way it lay, and a small piece may be examined while the operation continues.
statement.anatomy: The specimen is oriented and sent to pathology; frozen section may be taken when the diagnosis is uncertain, and the nerve (or a branch) is sacrificed only for malignancy, or rarely for repeatedly recurrent adenoma.

limitations: One institution’s practice; the protocol itself notes that the accuracy of frozen section has been debated and depends on the pathologist.
